is the least effective immunosuppressive agent in reversing recalcitrant rejection.
has been shown to prevent cardiac allograft vasculopathy.

stem: Azathioprine
options: is a macrolide antibiotic from Streptomyces tsukubaensis.
decreases the formation of interleukin-2.
causes a dose-related bone marrow suppression.
has been shown to prevent cardiac allograft vasculopathy
causes impaired glucose metabolism.

stem: Mycophenolate mofetil
options: inhibits a key step in the de novo biosynthesis of purines.
is inferior to azathioprine in reducing mortality after transplantation.
causes profound leukopenia compared to azathioprine.
is currently used in 25% of heart transplant recipients.
receiving cardiac transplant patients have higher levels of C-reactive protein.

stem: OKT3
options: is an equine monoclonal antibody directed against the chain of CD3 molecule.
facilitates the function of naive T cells.
has cytolytic effects on all circulating cells.
inhibits cytokine release syndrome.
is associated with the increased incidence of posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorders.

stem: Cardiac allograft rejection is the normal host response to cells recognized as nonself. Which of the following statements regarding acute cardiac rejection is correct?
options: The vast majority of cases are mediated by antibodies.
The highest risk factors are allografts from younger and female donors (irrespective of recipient sex).
In the cyclosporine era, the classical clinical manifestations of acute rejection are more frequently seen.
Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte count is the “gold standard” for diagnosis of acute rejection.
Azathioprine is the cornerstone of antirejection therapy.

stem: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) is a unique, rapidly progressive form of atherosclerosis in transplant recipients. CAV
options: is characterized in its early stages by luminal stenosis of epicardial branches.
angiographically is detected in approximately 90% of patients by 5 years after transplantation.
compared to atherosclerosis has concentric plaques.
is recognized by diffuse calcification of epicardial vessels.
is best treated by coronary artery bypass grafting.

stem: Cardiac retransplantation
options: accounts for 10% of the cardiac transplants currently performed.
actuarial survival at 3 years is 70%.
survival is better if the intertransplant interval is less than 6 months.
is associated with poor survival in older patients.
is primarily indicated for immunosuppression intolerance.

stem: Implantable left ventricular assist devices have benefited patients with end-stage heart failure as a bridge to cardiac transplantation. The Randomized Evaluation of Mechanical Assistance for the Treatment of Congestive Heart Failure (REMATCH) trial
options: randomized patients to receive a left ventricular assist device as destination therapy or cardiac transplantation
recruited patients with NYHA class III heart failure.
showed a reduction of 48 percent in the risk of death from any cause in the group that received left ventricular assist devices.
reported improved quality of life in patients on optimal medical therapy compared to those with left ventricular assist devices.
reported similar frequency of serious adverse events in the device group as that in the medical-therapy group.

stem: The overall goal of the SYNTAX trial is to assess the most appropriate revascularization strategy by randomizing patients to either (percutaneous intervention) PCI with TAXUS Express stents or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). At 3 years
options: major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events were elevated in the CABG arm.
rate of repeat revascularization was elevated in the CABG arm.
rates of the composite safety endpoint (death/stroke/myocardial infarction) were elevated in the PCI arm.
major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular event rates were not significantly different between arms in the left main stem subgroup.
major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular event rates were not significantly different between arms in the 3 vessel disease subgroup.

stem: Randomized On/Off Bypass (ROOBY) trial was funded by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Cooperative Studies Program to further assess the relative efficacy of on-pump and off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). The ROOBY trial
options: was a controlled, double-blind, randomized trial.
enrolled all-comers with no exclusion criteria.
showed that there was no significant difference between off-pump and on-pump CABG in the rate of the 30-day composite outcome.
showed that the proportion of patients with fewer grafts completed than originally planned was similar with off-pump and on-pump CABG.
showed that the rate of the 1-year composite outcome was higher for on-pump than for off-pump CABG.

stem: Aortic dissection is the most frequently diagnosed lethal condition of the aorta. Which one of the following statements regarding aortic dissection is correct?
options: Type B dissections occur with an overall greater frequency.
The intimal tear involves the full circumference of the aorta in majority of cases.
The primary tear in type A dissection is usually located on the left anterior aspect of the ascending aorta.
Retrograde type A dissection involves the coronary ostia in 50% of cases.
Myocardial ischemia and rupture into the pericardium are the cause of death in as many as 80% of deaths from acute dissection.

stem: The recently published 30 day outcomes of multicentre CORONARY trial that randomized 4752 patients to undergo on-pump or off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) suggest that
options: on-pump CABG is associated with significantly reduced rates of reoperation for bleeding compared to off-pump CABG.
on-pump CABG is associated with reduced mortality compared to off-pump CABG.
on-pump CABG resulted in more respiratory complications compared to off-pump CABG.
on-pump CABG resulted in more strokes compared to off-pump CABG.
on-pump CABG caused more new renal failure requiring dialysis compared to off-pump CABG.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding underlying concepts associated with cancer screening is correct?
options: Incidence is the number of cancers that exist in a defined population at a given point in time.
Incidence is expressed as cases per year per 100,000 individuals in the population.
Incidence is commonly expressed as cancers per 100,000 individuals in the population.
Prevalence is expressed as cases per year per 100,000 individuals in the population.
Prevalence refers to the number of cancer cases that develop during a defined period of time.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding chest x-ray screening trials for lung cancer is correct?
options: The Czechoslovakia randomized screening trial for lung cancer showed a significant increase in the number of cancers detected in the intervention group.
The design of all the National Cancer Institute (NCI) sponsored randomized clinical trials was similar.
The John Hopkins and Memorial Sloan-Kettering screening studies showed differences in the number of cancers detected.
The Memorial Sloan-Kettering screening study showed a mortality benefit.
The Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) trial detected only 10% stage I lung cancers.

stem: A 63-year-old male patient with an incidentally discovered solitary pulmonary nodule in the upper lobe of right lung on a routine chest radiograph was recommended to undergo 18F-FDG PET scan for further assessment of this nodule. Which of the following statements about the inherent limitations of 18F-FDG PET scan is true?
options: Bronchoalveolar carcinoma has a strong avidity for 18F-FDG.
False-negative findings are most commonly associated with uptake of 18F-FDG in infectious or inflammatory tissue.
18F-FDG PET for cancer imaging has a limited reconstructed spatial resolution of 4–10 mm in available commercial systems.
18F-FDG PET is considered the investigation of first choice for assessment of possible cerebral metastases from known primary neoplasms.
Infection imaging with 18F-FDG PET relies on the fact that granulocytes and mononuclear cells use glucose as an energy source at all times.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the role of 18F-FDG PET scan for diagnosis of lung cancer is true?
options: Availability of 18F-FDG PET obviates the need for conventional work-up for the diagnosis and staging of lung cancer.
18F-FDG PET scan has no proven benefit in patients at low-risk for lung cancer.
18F-FDG PET will be most useful in patients at a high risk of lung cancer.
For detection of mediastinal lymph node metastases, CT has a superior sensitivity and specificity compared to 18F-FDG PET.
In low-risk patients, the negative predictive value of 18F-FDG PET is extremely high.

stem: Chest CT scan of a 47-year-old male revealed the presence of a solitary pulmonary nodule in the left lower lobe. Which of the following morphologic characteristics is highly suggestive of malignancy?
options: Central nodular calcification
Diffuse calcification
Laminated calcification
Popcorn like calcification
Stippled calcification

stem: A 52-year-old smoker requires a left upper lobectomy for a peripheral T1N0 squamous cell lung cancer. Which of the following pulmonary function study results would indicate that the patient would be at very high risk for postoperative pulmonary complications?
options: a DLCO of 70% of predicted with an FEV1 of 1.4 liters
an FEV1 of 1.5 liters and an arterial blood gas demonstrating a pO2 of 72mmHg, a pCO2 of 38 mmHg and a pH of 7.40
an FEV1 of 1.4 liters, an MVV of 55% of predicted and a VO2 max of 20 cc per kilogram per minute.
a quantitative ventilation-perfusion scan demonstrating 70% perfusion to the right lung with an FEV1 of 1.4 liters and a VO2 max of 8 cc per kilogram per minute.
a quantitative ventilation-perfusion scan demonstrating 80% perfusion to the right lung with an FEV1 of 1.3 liters and a VO2 max of 15 cc per kilogram per minute

stem: A 64-year-old man developed severe respiratory failure and adult respiratory distress syndrome following lung resection for lung cancer requiring mechanical ventilatory support. A CT scan demonstrates pneumatoceles. This complication of mechanical ventilation may have been prevented by
options: decreasing positive end expiratory pressure.
increasing tidal volume.
instituting pressure control ventilation.
pharmacologic muscle paralysis.
reducing the fractional inspired oxygen concentration.

stem: Cervical mediastinoscopy is a common procedure used for the diagnosis of mediastinal disease and the staging of lung cancer. Although complications of cervical mediastinoscopy are uncommon, the most common major complication is
options: airway disruption.
esophageal perforation.
hemorrhage.
recurrent nerve palsy.
stroke.

stem: Traumatic diaphragmatic injuries are uncommon events but are associated with a high mortality. Which of the following statements regarding injury to the diaphragm is true?
options: Blunt injury to the diaphragm is more likely to involve the right side.
Delayed recognition of diaphragmatic injury is more common after penetrating trauma than blunt injury.
Repair of acute diaphragm injuries is better handled using a transthoracic approach.
Repair of chronic diaphragm injuries (greater than three months) is best accomplished abdominally.
The most common finding on the standard x-ray after penetrating injury is elevation of the affected diaphragm.

stem: Massive hemoptysis is one of the most dreaded of all respiratory emergencies and can have a variety of underlying causes. In 90% of cases, the source of massive hemoptysis is the bronchial circulation. Which of the following statements about bronchial artery anatomy is correct?
options: Aberrant bronchial arteries enter the pulmonary parenchyma through the adherent pleura or via the pulmonary ligament.
Nonbronchial systemic collateral vessels cannot be angiographically differentiated from aberrant bronchial arteries.
The bronchial arteries originate directly from the ascending thoracic aorta, most commonly between the levels of the T2 and T3 vertebrae.
The bronchial arteries only supply the intrapulmonary airways and bronchovascular bundles.
The majority of aberrant bronchial arteries originate from the aortic arch.

stem: Hemoptysis may be a life-threatening condition with an inclination to recur if definitive treatment is not instituted. Massive hemoptysis
options: is defined as expectoration of blood of more than 200 mL per day.
is most commonly caused by non small cell lung cancer in the Third World.
is best managed medically with low rate of recurrence.
managed with bronchial artery embolization may not be successful in 10% to 25% of patients.
must be managed surgically in all patients.

stem: A 52-year-old patient with localized bronchiectasis of right lower lobe presents with a third documented episode of hemoptysis. Within six hours the bleeding stops. One month ago the FEV1 was 1.5 liters. The best management for this patient is
options: bronchoscopy followed by angiography with arterial embolization.
continued observation in the intensive care unit for another 48 hours and if no further bleeding occurs discharge to home on antibiotics.
resection of the involved area.
treatment with anti-fungal chemotherapy for six weeks.
treatment with rotating bactericidal antibiotics.

stem: A 62-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history has had repeated episodes of “bronchitis” characterized by a cough productive of purulent sputum. He presents now with hemoptysis which began six hours ago. He produces 100 ml of blood with the first cough you witness and he then continues to bring up blood every time he coughs. His chest x-ray shows a cavitating lesion in the right upper lobe. He had one previous episode of hemoptysis within the past year which was managed by his family doctor. Pulmonary function studies performed three months ago demonstrated an FEV1 of 2.2 liters (60% predicted). What should be the initial management of this patient?
options: angiography for bronchial arterial embolization.
bronchoscopy followed by thoracotomy and lobectomy.
flexible bronchoscopy with mainstem bronchial intubation with an endotracheal tube.
intensive care unit observation, sedation, anti-tussive medication and bedrest with the bleeding side down.
rigid bronchoscopy with insertion of a balloon occlusion catheter.

stem: Which of the following represents the most common cause of esophageal perforation/rupture?
options: blunt trauma (deceleration and steering wheel).
esophageal instrumentation (iatrogenic).
foreign body aspiration/impaction.
penetrating civilian trauma.
spontaneous post-emetic rupture (Boerhaave‘s Syndrome).

stem: The best management for a patient with a distal esophageal perforation which occurs 48 hours prior to presentation is
options: antibiotics and proper drainage.
diversion and exclusion.
extensive debridement with T-tube controlled fistula.
primary repair with buttressing.
resection with cervical stoma, gastrostomy, and jejunostomy.

stem: Fistula formation between the innominate artery and the trachea is a rare but potentially catastrophic complication after tracheostomy. Which of the following statements regarding tracheoinnominate artery fistula (TIF) is correct?
options: TIF associated bleeding can be temporarily stopped in 100% of cases with overinflating the tracheostomy tube cuff.
TIF associated bleeding is best confirmed by flexible bronchoscopy.
TIF formation is seen with low-lying tracheostomy sites typically below the third tracheal ring.
TIF in most cases presents as sentinel bleed.
TIF in most cases usually occurs within a week of placement of tracheostomy tube.

stem: A 14-year-old ventilator-dependent girl with a history of anoxic brain injury and a tracheostomy in-situ for 6 months suddenly develops massive bleeding from her tracheostomy site. Which of the following is the best initial management in this case?
options: Chest radiograph to exclude pneumonia as a cause of massive hemoptysis.
Flexible bronchoscopy to visualize the site of bleeding.
Insertion of Fogarty balloon catheter via the brachial artery into the innominate artery under radiograph guidance to achieve tamponade after balloon dilation.
Resection of the innominate artery with preservation of the right carotid-right subclavian junction.
The tracheostomy tube cuff should be hyperinflated.

stem: Which of the following is the second most common tracheal tumor?
options: adenoid cystic carcinoma.
carcinoid.
granular cell tumor.
mucoepidermoid tumor.
mucus gland adenocarcinoma.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) of the trachea is correct?
options: Primary tracheal ACC is an aggressive tumor.
Primary tracheal ACC is commonly seen in the third decade.
Primary tracheal ACC is predominantly found in men.
Primary tracheal ACC of distal trachea has a worse prognosis.
Primary tracheal ACC spreads most commonly by lymphatic metastases.

stem: A 46-year-old patient was found to have a one centimeter squamous cell cancer of the mid trachea. The patient was treated with 6000 cGy. Two years later the patient is found to have an eight millimeter local recurrence. The best management of this patient is
options: brachytherapy.
cis-platinum based chemotherapy.
laser ablation.
tracheal resection and omental wrap.
tracheal stent.

stem: Which of the following arteries is the principle blood supply to the upper two thirds of the trachea?
options: external carotid.
inferior thyroid.
internal thoracic.
superior thyroid.
transverse cervical.

stem: Ten days after an extensive tracheal resection, a patient developed sudden massive subcutaneous emphysema and respiratory distress. The patient was intubated with great difficulty. At exploration complete dehiscence of the trachea is found. The best management of this patient is
options: antibiotic therapy alone.
hilar and laryngeal release, and reanastomosis-with muscle flap buttress.
oral intubation and suction drainage through the neck.
tracheal stent and muscle flap buttress.
T-tube.

stem: Which of the following is a recognized risk factor for anastomotic complications after tracheal resection?
options: diabetes
idiopathic laryngotracheal stenosis
postintubation tracheal stenosis
tracheoesophageal fistula
tumor

stem: An elderly patient has been intubated and ventilated for two weeks for severe bilateral pneumonia. A nasogastric tube is in place for feedings. The patient is found to have a tracheoesophageal fistula involving the upper third of the trachea. Endoscopy reveals a circumferential area of tracheal damage from a cuff injury and a one centimeter tracheoesophageal fistula. Which of the following is part of the initial management of this problem?
options: esophageal diversion
gastrostomy tube
local division of the fistula with strap muscle interposition
T-tube placement and removal of the nasogastric tube
tracheal resection and fistula repair with strap muscle interposition

stem: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the bronchus is similar to its counterpart arising from the salivary glands but does have some distinct characteristics of its own. Which of the following statements regarding bronchial mucoepidermoid carcinoma is correct?
options: It accounts for approximately 15% of primary lung tumors.
It has a predilection for females.
It is predominantly seen in the elderly population.
It is typically diagnosed by conventional radiography.
It typically arises from the large airways.

stem: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the bronchus is a rare primary lung malignancy. It is
options: characterized by reduced production of mucoepidermoid carcinoma translocated 1– mastermind-like 2 (MECT1-MAML2).
differentiated from adenocarcinoma by immunoperoxidase staining with antibodies to cytokeratin 7 and thyroid transcription factor 1.
not known to recur once completely excised.
predominantly caused by reciprocal translocation involving chromosome X.
surgically treated by pneumonectomy.

stem: Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the tracheobronchial tree is quite uncommon. Which of the following statements regarding bronchial adenoid cystic carcinoma is correct?
options: It has an aggressive course.
It has a low rate of recurrence.
It has an early onset of distant metastases.
The most common histologic type is the cribriform pattern.
The cribriform histology has a poor prognosis.

stem: After a complete resection, the most important factor influencing survival in patients with carcinoid tumors of lung is
options: cell type (typical versus atypical).
location of the tumor (peripheral versus central).
postoperative radiation therapy.
presence of N1 disease.
tumor size.

stem: A 50-year-old man with six months history of dyspnoea and hemoptysis was found to have a solitary, well-demarcated radiopaque mass in the left upper lobe with associated atelectasis. Flexible bronchoscopy revealed a sessile, smooth, yellow-pink, lobulated lesion, with intact overlying surface mucosa in the left upper lobe bronchus. Bronchoscopic biopsy of the mass was reported as composed of groups or sheets of small, uniform cells arranged in a trabecular pattern, supported by a rich fibrovascular stroma. Lymphatic or vascular invasion was absent, and no focal necrosis was seen. Cells were oval or spindle shaped with amphophilic cytoplasm, finely stippled chromatin, and occasionally nucleoid. Nuclear pleomorphism was not seen, and cells were predominantly diploid with a low proliferation index (<7% in S-phase). Which of the following statements about this tumor is true?
options: Cytoproliferative activity in this tumor is generally very high.
High-molecular weight cytokeratins are typically found in this tumor.
It usually arises in the fifth decade.
There is a strong association with smoking.
This tumor accounts for 20% of all lung malignancies.

stem: Chest radiograph of a 40-year-old man showed a smooth, well-circumscribed peripheral pulmonary nodule measuring 2.5 cm. Computerized tomography revealed the presence of “popcorn calcifications” in the nodule. The solitary pulmonary nodule is most likely a
options: Granular cell tumor
Hamartoma
Hemangioma
Lymphangioma
Typical carcinoid tumor

stem: A 35-year-old man had a solitary pulmonary nodule removed from his left upper lobe after a parenchymal sparing pulmonary resection. The histology was reported as benign neoplasm composed of large ovoid or polygonal cells that took up periodic acid-Schiff stain. The solitary pulmonary nodule is most likely a
options: Granular cell tumor
Hamartoma
Hemangioma
Lymphangioma
Typical carcinoid tumor

stem: Chest radiograph of a 43-year-old man showed a sharply circumscribed peripheral pulmonary nodule measuring 2.5 cm. There was strong contrast enhancement of the lesion on computerized tomography. The solitary pulmonary nodule is most likely a(n)
options: Arteriovenous malformation
Hamartoma
Hemangioma
Lymphangioma
Typical carcinoid tumor

stem: Which of the following characteristics of a solitary pulmonary nodule is associated with the highest likelihood of malignancy?
options: Age 60-69 years
Lobulated mass
Not calcified
PET SUR >2.5
Spiculated mass

stem: A 62-year-old patient with a 50 pack-year history of smoking was referred to thoracic surgical outpatient clinic with cough of four weeks duration productive of whitish sputum. A chest radiograph showed a lower lobe mass and the chest computed tomographic (CT) scan demonstrated extensive lymphadenopathy, both ipsilateral and contralateral, and a central mass lesion. Biopsy from bronchoscopy showed molding of the cells with the “salt and pepper” chromatin pattern and scant cytoplasm. The metastatic work-up was negative. The best treatment is
options: high dose radiation therapy.
thoracotomy and lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection followed by postoperative radiation therapy.
treatment with cis-platinum and etoposide.
treatment with velban, bleomycin and cis-platinum.
two cycles of cis-platinum and etoposide with concurrent radiation therapy followed by thoracotomy.

stem: A 58-year-old ex-smoker was referred to thoracic surgical outpatient clinic with cough of four weeks duration productive of whitish sputum. Chest x-ray demonstrated a < 3 cm coin lesion. The chest computed tomogram was performed which demonstrated no mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Needle biopsy of the pulmonary nodule demonstrated a small cell lung cancer. After an extent of disease evaluation (including mediastinoscopy) demonstrated no evidence of metastases, the treatment should include
options: chemotherapy only.
chemotherapy plus radiation therapy.
radiation therapy only.
resection plus chemotherapy.
resection plus radiation therapy.

stem: Following cervical mediastinoscopy, a 56-year-old patient underwent a right upper lobectomy for a 4 cm (T2) squamous cell carcinoma of the lung. The final pathology report notes that two of five intraparenchymal lymph nodes (N1) were positive for metastatic tumor. Which of the following statements regarding adjuvant therapy is true?
options: Adjuvant Bacillus Calmette-Guerin improves local control.
Adjuvant chemotherapy is detrimental to survival.
Adjuvant radiation therapy improves local control.
Adjuvant radiation therapy improves survival.
Predicted three year survival without adjuvant therapy is 70%.

stem: A 56-year-old patient had successful resection of a stage II non small cell lung cancer. The single factor most predictive of survival in this patient with a completely resected stage II non-small cell lung cancer is
options: neoadjuvant radiation therapy.
number of metastatic N1 lymph nodes.
postoperative radiation therapy.
T status (T1 versus T2).
visceral pleural invasion.

stem: A 58-year-old patient underwent a right lower lobectomy with chest wall resection for a 2 cm non-small cell lung cancer involving the lateral aspect of the seventh rib. Pathologic examination of the specimen revealed negative lymph nodes and a negative margin. The best postoperative management for this patient is
options: chemotherapy.
chemotherapy and radiation therapy.
observation.
radiation therapy.
resection of seventh vertebra.

stem: A 52-year-old ex-smoker with adenocarcinoma of the right upper lobe has microscopically positive contralateral (4L) lymph nodes (American Thoracic Society staging criteria) at mediastinoscopy. The best management plan is
options: induction chemotherapy with cis-platinum and vinblastine followed by thoracotomy and lobectomy.
radiation therapy to 69.6 Gy given in a twice daily fractionation regimen.
standard fractionation radiation therapy given concurrently with vinblastine and cis-platinum.
standard fractionation radiation therapy given concurrently with vinblastine and cis-platinum followed by thoracotomy and pulmonary resection.
thoracotomy with lobectomy and complete mediastinal lymph node dissection.

stem: The computerized tomographic scanning of the chest and upper abdomen in 58-year-old ex-smoker with a biopsy proven non-small cell lung cancer (clinical T1N0) demonstrated an enlarged left adrenal gland. To evaluate this mass, the next diagnostic step is
options: abdominal ultrasound.
laparoscopy.
magnetic resonance imaging.
needle biopsy.
resection.

stem: A 52-year-old patient with an otherwise operable non-small cell lung cancer (T2N0) was found to have a solitary mass on brain computed tomography. The optimal treatment for this patient is
options: radiation therapy to brain and lung.
radiation therapy to brain and resection of lung disease.
radiation therapy to brain and systemic chemotherapy;
resection of both the brain metastasis and lung disease.
resection of the brain metastasis and radiation therapy to lung.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding T4 non small cell lung cancer is correct?
options: Limited local invasion of the intrapericardial pulmonary artery or left atrium can be resected completely with expected 5-year survival rates of ≈ 50%.
Superior vena cava resection is the most accepted extended vascular resection for T4 disease with 5-year survival rates ranging from 40% to 50%
Systemic arterial (aorta) and esophageal invasion of T4 lung cancer carry the best long-term outcome.
T4 lung cancers invading the vertebral body can be resected with a 5-year survival rate of 15%
Vascular resection and reconstruction of the aorta and left atrium have been safely described with 5-year survival rates of 40%.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding chemotherapy for patients with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer is correct?
options: Cisplatin-based chemotherapy regimens are superior compared to carboplatin-based regimens.
The addition of a third chemotherapeutic agent to existing doublets improves survival.
The overall therapeutic efficacy improves with the two chemotherapeutic agents with no significant cost in toxicity or quality of life compared to single agent.
The response rate with two chemotherapeutic agents is similar to that with single agent.
The survival rates with single chemotherapeutic agents are similar to those with two chemotherapeutic agents.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding addition of molecular-targeted agents to established standard double chemotherapeutic agents for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is correct?
options: Erlotinib in combination with carboplatin-paclitaxel improves survival in all patients with advanced NSCLC.
Erlotinib in combination with carboplatin-paclitaxel improves survival in patients with advanced NSCLC with no history of smoking.
Gefitinib in combination and carboplatin-paclitaxel improves survival in all patients with advanced NSCLC.
Gefitinib in combination with cisplatin-gemcitabine improves survival in all patients with advanced NSCLC.
Gefitinib in combination with cisplatin-gemcitabine improves survival in patients with advanced NSCLC with strong history of smoking.

stem: The stage-specific selection of therapy is the standard for patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Investigation of the molecular biology of lung cancer has provided pathways and targets that may be used to improve the efficacy of therapy and improve the survival for patients with lung cancer. Which of the following statements regarding molecular staging and the selection of therapy for non-small cell lung cancer?
options: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFr) expression is associated with increased response to chemotherapy and radiotherapy.
Gefitinib is indicated as monotherapy in advanced NSCLC after failure of both platinum-based and docetaxel chemotherapies.
Ligand binding to p53 results in receptor dimerization, autophosphorylation, activation of cytoplasmic proteins, and eventually DNA synthesis.
Studies that evaluate molecular prognostic variables must be limited to the inclusion of patients with advanced-stage disease.
The proto-oncogene c-erbB-1is a tumor suppressor nuclear phosphoprotein.

stem: The human p53 protein is a tumor suppressor nuclear phosphoprotein. Which of the following statements regarding p53 protein is correct?
options: Adenoviral p53 gene therapy combined with radiotherapy in patients with advanced NSCLC is associated with an improved pathologic control rate.
Adenoviral p53 gene therapy is associated with improved survival in patients with NSCLC.
Deletion or mutation of p53 genes is associated with good prognosis in patients with non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC).
Deletion or mutation of p53 genes makes patients more sensitive to chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
p53 activates the growth-arrest pathway to allow DNA repair or the apoptotic pathway leading to programmed cell death.

stem: Cyclooxygenase enzymes function to convert arachidonic acids to prostaglandins. Which of the following statements regarding cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) is correct?
options: Addition of celecoxib to paclitaxel and carboplatin may enhance the response to preoperative paclitaxel and carboplatin in patients with NSCLC compared with historical controls.
COX-2 expression is associated with decreased tumor invasion, angiogenesis, and metastasis.
Combination of COX-2 inhibitors and platinum compounds reduces the cytotoxicity of platinum compounds in NSCLC cell lines.
Combination of COX-2 inhibitors and platinum compounds results in complete pathologic responses in patients with stages IB to IIIA non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
The cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) enzyme produces prostacyclin, which stimulates bcl-2 and thus inhibits apoptosis.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding molecular biology of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is correct?
options: Matrix metalloproteinases (MMP) enhance vascular barriers.

Therapy with recombinant humanized anti-vascular endothelial growth factor antibodies (rhuMAb VEGF) alone is associated with improved response rates and prolonged time to disease progression in in patients with advanced NSCLC compared with chemotherapy.

The use of marimastat, the first orally available synthetic matrix metalloproteinase inhibitor (MMPI), is associated with survival benefit and prolongation in time to disease progression for patients with NSCLC.
Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is strongly induced by hypoxia.
VEGF reduces vascular permeability.

stem: A 50-year-old patient had successful complete resection of superior sulcus non-small cell lung cancer. Following successful resection, the most important predictor of survival is
options: histology.
intra-operative brachytherapy.
nodal status.
pre-operative radiation therapy.
postoperative radiation therapy.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the anatomy of the superior sulcus is correct?
options: The apical pleura is the superior most structure in the interscalene compartment.
The dorsal scapular artery is present in the interscalene compartment.
The subclavian artery is posterior to the middle scalene muscle.
The subclavian vein is posterior to the anterior scalene muscle.
The trunks of the brachial plexus are anterior to the anterior scalene muscle.

stem:
The chest radiograph below shows left-sided superior sulcus tumor in a 48-year-old male.
Which of the following findings on further imaging of the chest will suggest that resection of this tumor is possible?
options: distant metastatic disease
invasion of the brachial plexus roots
invasion of more than 50% of a vertebral body
invasion of the esophagus
tumor adherent to T1 nerve

stem: Which of the following statements regarding surgical approaches for resection of superior sulcus tumor is correct?
options: Anterior transcervical-thoracic approach prevents glenohumeral instability and functional discomfort.
Pneumonectomy is easy to perform through the anterior transcervical-thoracic approach compared to Shaw-Paulson approach.
Posterolateral thoracotomy enables safe excision of tumor involving the subclavian vein.
Shaw-Paulson approach provides excellent access to the middle and anterior compartments of the thoracic inlet.
The combined use of both an anterior and a posterolateral approach is associated with a higher mortality than the use of either approach alone.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding detection and treatment of small intraepithelial and microinvasive preinvasive lesions of lung is correct?
options: Autofluorescence bronchoscopy is more specific than white light bronchoscopy at detecting carcinoma in situ.
Photodynamic therapy produces tumor death by thermal injury.
Photodynamic therapy results in a 98% complete response in early lung lesions ≥ 2 cm
Recurrence rate following photodynamic therapy for small superficial squamous cell carcinoma is 30%.
The use of high-dose brachytherapy in three to six sessions results in response rates superior to photodynamic therapy.

stem: Which of the following is the most frequent cause of perioperative mortality following bronchoplastic procedures?
options: bronchopleural fistula.
bronchovascular fistula.
empyema.
pulmonary embolism.
respiratory failure.

stem: A 55-year-old patient with an FEV1 of 2.0 liters had a sleeve lobectomy for a squamous cell carcinoma that involved the origin of the right upper lobe orifice. On the fifth postoperative day, the patient developed a temperature of 39.0°C and abruptly coughed up 125 ml of blood. Bronchoscopy reveals an area of partial necrosis at the anastomosis with fresh clot. The best management is
options: immediate bronchoscopic placement of an endobronchial stent.
immediate redo thoracotomy and completion pneumonectomy.
immediate redo thoracotomy and wrapping of the anastomosis with intercostal muscle.
neodymium-YAG laser ablation of the bleeding area.
observation and antibiotics.

stem: A 56-year-old patient with FEV1 = 3 liters underwent a right carinal pneumonectomy for a squamous carcinoma involving the carinal spur. The anastomosis was performed with interrupted 4-0 Vicryl® and covered with a pleural flap. Which of the following complications is most likely to occur and to be fatal in this patient?
options: airway stenosis.
bronchopleural fistula.
bronchovascular fistula.
dehiscence at the bronchus.
post-pneumonectomy pulmonary edema.

stem: A patient with a T1N0 lung cancer and diminished pulmonary reserve needs a pulmonary resection. In making a decision to perform segmentectomy rather than lobectomy, many factors need to be considered. Which of the following characteristics of segmentectomy is correct?
options: equivalent local recurrence rate when compared to lobectomy
fewer pleural space complications when performed without a stapler compared to lobectomy
reduced air leakage when performed with the classic stripping technique compared to lobectomy
reduced mortality compared to lobectomy patients
similar pulmonary function one year after operation compared to lobectomy

stem: The Medical Research Council LU22 trial investigating whether, in patients with operable non-small cell lung cancer of any stage, outcomes could be improved by giving platinum-based chemotherapy before surgery showed that
options: preoperative chemotherapy did not alter the type or completeness of the surgery.
preoperative chemotherapy failed to downstage the tumors.
preoperative chemotherapy increased postoperative complications.
preoperative chemotherapy negatively impacted the quality of life.
preoperative chemotherapy produced a benefit in terms of overall survival.

stem: The postoperative radiotherapy (PORT) meta-analysis evaluates the effect of postoperative radiotherapy on survival and recurrence in patients with completely resected non-small cell lung cancer. The meta-analysis
options: showed a significant adverse effect of PORT on survival.
showed that PORT improved survival in younger patients.
showed that PORT was increasingly detrimental with higher nodal status.
showed that PORT was most detrimental for patients with stage III disease.
showed that the effects of PORT were more detrimental in those patients with stage II than with stage I disease.

stem: A 36-year-old patient is to undergo resection of a solitary metastasis from an extremity soft tissue sarcoma. When considering a patient for resection of pulmonary metastases from soft-tissue sarcoma, the factor which most strongly predicts survival is
options: disease-free interval.
number of metastases.
resectability.
tumor doubling time.
unilaterality versus bilaterality.

stem: The International Registry of Lung Metastases was established in 1991 to assess the long-term results of pulmonary metastasectomy. Analysis of the data collected by International registry shows that
options: the disease-free interval is not a significant prognostic factor.
the number of metastases has no impact on survival.
the patients with germ cell tumors have the worst survival.
the survival after a second metastasectomy is remarkably good.
the survivals of patients with epithelial tumors and sarcomas differ significantly.

stem: The chest radiograph shown below was obtained on postoperative day 2 in a 56-year-old man after right pneumonectomy for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. Which of the following statements is correct about the condition shown on the chest radiograph?
options: It has a reported prevalence of 20%.
It is associated with high serum colloidal osmotic pressure.
It is associated with a mortality rate of 2.5%-5%.
It is diagnosed primarily through a process of exclusion.
It occurs more commonly after left pneumonectomy.

stem:
The chest radiographs shown below were obtained (A) on postoperative day 18 and (B) postoperative day 20 in a ventilated 65-year-old man after right pneumonectomy for large cell carcinoma.
Which of the following statements is correct about the condition shown on the chest radiographs?
options: It is most commonly seen after lymph node sampling.
It is most commonly seen on the left side.
It more often occurs within the first two weeks after surgery.
The condition is best managed surgically.
The most common cause of death associated with this condition is empyema.

stem:
The chest radiograph and CT image shown below were obtained in a 35-year-old woman who presented to the Accident & Emergency Department complaining of exertional dyspnea, inspiratory stridor, and recurrent pulmonary infections. She had previously undergone right pneumonectomy for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis 11 months ago.
What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia
Esophagobronchial fistula
Late-onset postpneumonectomy bronchopleural fistula
Late-onset postpneumonectomy empyema
Postpneumonectomy syndrome

stem: Which of the following statements regarding broncholithiasis is correct?
options: A broncholith is usually formed by aspiration of bone tissue or in situ calcification of aspirated foreign material.
Bronchoscopy is contraindicated for removal of broncholiths.
Bronchoscopy often fails to aid in diagnosis.
Lithoptysis is the most common mode of presentation of broncholithiasis.
The treatment of choice for asymptomatic calcified nodes is surgery.

stem: Localized fibrous tumors of the pleura (LFTP) are uncommon neoplasms that have gained increasing recognition over the last 2 decades as a discrete pathologic entity. Which of the following statements about LFTP is correct?
options: LFTP are associated with prior asbestos exposure.
LFTP are predominantly seen in men.
LFTP arise from the mesothelial lining of the pleura.
LFTP have a peak incidence in the second to third decades.
LFTP patients predominantly are symptomatic at presentation.

stem: A 56-year-old man with hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy and hypoglycaemia was noted to have a solid, well-circumscribed mass located at the periphery of the lung field adjacent to the chest wall on plain chest radiograph. The most likely diagnosis is
options: bronchial adenoid cystic carcinoma
bronchial carcinoid
bronchial mucoepidermoid carcinoma
hamartoma
localized fibrous tumor of the pleura

stem: Recent advances in immunohistochemical techniques have allowed pathologists to further differentiate localized fibrous tumors of the pleura (LFTP) from other similar neoplasms through the development of a relatively unique profile for this tumor. Which of the following immunohistochemical marker is absent in LFTP?
options: Bcl-2
CD34
CD99
Keratin
Vimentin

stem: Complete surgical resection is the treatment of choice for benign and malignant localized fibrous tumors of the pleura (LFTP), with 1 to 2 cm margins if possible. Which of the following statements regarding the rates of tumor recurrence for LFTP is correct?
options: Patients with benign pedunculated tumors have the highest rate of recurrence.
Patients with benign sessile tumors have the highest rate of recurrence.
Patients with malignant pedunculated tumors have the highest rate of recurrence.
Patients with malignant sessile tumors have the highest rate of recurrence.
There is no difference in the rates of recurrence for different histologic types of LFTP.

stem: BTS (British Thoracic Society) randomized feasibility study of active symptom control with or without chemotherapy in malignant pleural mesothelioma: ISRCTN 54469112 showed that
options: a phase III trial comparing ASC with or without chemotherapy is not feasible.
chemotherapy with vinorelbine was superior compared to MVP regimen.
clinically relevant levels of palliation were achieved with ASC only.
randomisation to active symptom control (ASC) with or without chemotherapy was unacceptable to patients.
the EORTC QL questionnaire was inferior to FACT-L in terms of completeness of data and patient preference.

stem: The randomised trial in malignant mesothelioma (M) of early (E) versus delayed (D) chemotherapy in symptomatically stable patients (MED trial) showed that
options: delayed use of chemotherapy resulted in better maintenance of quality of life.
early use of chemotherapy had no effect on progression of symptoms.
early use of chemotherapy offered survival advantage.
median time to symptomatic progression was the same in both groups.
more health resources were used as a result of delayed use of chemotherapy.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding myasthenia gravis is correct?
options: In myasthenia gravis patients present with generalized fatigue or pain.
In myasthenia gravis ptosis is generally symmetrical.
In ocular myasthenia gravis papillary function is abnormal.
Isolated oropharyngeal or limb weakness is the most common initial presentation.
The onset of myasthenia gravis is influenced by gender and age in a bimodal fashion.

stem: A 28-year-old-female is diagnosed with myasthenia gravis. Which of the following statements regarding the etiology of myasthenia gravis is correct?
options: Autoimmune myasthenia gravis results from antibody-mediated, B cell-dependent immunologic attack on the postsynaptic membrane of the neuromuscular junction.
In most cases, antibodies bind to the main immunogenic region of the β-subunit of the acetylcholine receptor.
In myasthenia gravis damage to the postsynaptic membrane results in upregulation of acetylcholine receptors.
Patients with seronegative and ocular myasthenia gravis are more likely to have thymomas.
Thymomas are present in 10% of patients with myasthenia gravis.

stem: Thymoma is a rare neoplasm usually with an indolent growth pattern. Which of the following statements regarding thymoma is correct?
options: Thymoma constitutes 90% of all mediastinal tumors.
Thymoma is an epithelial tumor.
Thymoma is predominantly seen in early teens.
Thymoma is most commonly associated with hypogammaglobulinemia.
Thymoma primarily affects females.

stem: Which of the following is the radiologic examination of choice for evaluation of all mediastinal masses in the anterior compartment?
options: Chest CT scan with intravenous contrast
Chest x-ray
Echocardiography
Fluoroscopy
Positron Emission Tomography

stem: Thymomas are classified according to their neoplastic (epithelial) and nonneoplastic (lymphocyte) components. It is not uncommon to have more than one histologic subtype within a single tumor. Which of the following statements regarding histology of thymomas is correct?
options: The spindled epithelial cells of type A thymoma express the B-cell marker CD20.
Type A thymoma has abundant lymphocytes.
The type A thymomas have ovoid or polygonal epithelial cells and immature, cortical-type (double CD4+ 8+, CD1a+, TdT+) thymocytes.
Type A thymomas are significantly more likely to be higher stage than type B thymomas.
The type B thymoma has neoplastic epithelial cells that assume an elongated or spindle cell appearance.

stem: Type B thymomas are further subdivided into three subtypes B1, B2, and B3. Which of the following statements regarding these subtypes of type B thymomas is correct?
options: A hallmark of type B2 thymoma is the presence of focal medullary differentiation.
Cortical-type (double CD4+ 8+, CD1a+, TdT+) thymocytes are most abundant in type B3 thymoma.
Type B1 has the highest ratio of epithelial cells to thymocytes.
Type B2 has the highest ratio of epithelial cells to thymocytes.
Type B3 has the highest ratio of epithelial cells to thymocytes.

stem: A 52-year-old man was diagnosed with a stage III B thymoma. Stage III B thymoma
options: has microscopic transcapsular invasion.
has macroscopic invasion into surrounding fatty tissue or grossly adherent to but not through mediastinal pleura or pericardium.
has macroscopic invasion into neighboring organs (i.e., pericardium, great vessels, lung) without invasion of great vessels.
has macroscopic invasion into neighboring organs (i.e., pericardium, great vessels, lung) with invasion of great vessels.
is macroscopically and microscopically completely encapsulated.

stem: Which of the following statements about the prognosis of thymic tumors is correct?
options: Myasthenia gravis is a negative prognostic factor for long-term survival.
There is no difference in survival between between Masaoka Stage I, II, and III.
There is significant difference in survival between Masaoka Stage III and IV.
The size of thymoma does not influence survival.
The WHO histology does not influence survival.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding thymic tumors is correct?
options: Chemotherapy results in complete cure of stage IV thymic tumors.
Response rates to chemotherapy in the metastatic setting range from 30% to 60%.
The majority of patients with thymic tumors present with late stage disease.
Thymic tumors are predominantly non-surgical diseases.
Thymic tumors are resistant to chemotherapy.

stem: A 59-year-old man was diagnosed with malignant thymoma. Which of the following statements regarding malignant thymomas is correct?
options: Intrathoracic recurrence can develop after complete surgical resection in up to 40% of those with invasive disease.
Invasive thymomas are radioresistant.
Malignant thymomas are usually rapidly-growing tumors with an aggressive natural history.
Patients with Masaoka stage II disease with fibrous adhesion to the mediastinal pleura have similar recurrence rates to those without fibrous adhesions to the mediastinal pleura.
Postoperative radiation therapy decreases the incidence of subsequent pleural dissemination in completely resected invasive thymoma.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the treatment of thymic tumors is correct?
options: For locally advanced, large, invasive thymomas that are unresectable or marginally resectable, preoperative adjuvant radiation therapy fails to render it resectable.
For stage III/IV disease, the evidence supporting the use of postoperative radiation therapy is lacking.
Induction chemotherapy may be effective at down-staging thymoma.
Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery and adjuvant radiotherapy has no impact on the survival of patients with locally advanced thymoma.
Postoperative radiotherapy for thymic carcinoma offers a survival benefit.

stem: A 36-year-old man with chest discomfort had a chest radiograph that showed a well-defined lobulated mass in the anterosuperior mediastinum. Full blood count revealed pure red cell aplasia. Further evaluation with contrast-enhanced thoracic CT scanning (Figure) revealed a mass with a heterogenous high-attenuated solid upper portion (arrow) with a small calcification in the left anterior aspect of the main pulmonary artery. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Benign mediastinal teratoma
Invasive thymoma
Mediastinal goiter
Mediastinal parathyroid adenoma
Mediastinal seminoma

stem: A 45-year-old male complaining of cough and shortness of breath had a contrast-enhanced CT scan showing a necrotic mass with an irregularly shaped enhancing wall in the right anterior mediastinum (Figure). CT-guided biopsy of the mass showed a predominance of lymphoepitheliomatous cell types with high-grade atypia, necrosis, and > 10 mitoses per high-power field. Clinical examination was unremarkable. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Benign mediastinal teratoma
Mediastinal goiter
Mediastinal parathyroid adenoma
Mediastinal seminoma
Thymic carcinoma

stem: A 16-year-old boy with new onset cough had a chest x-ray that showed mediastinal widening. CT scan (Figure) showed a heterogeneous left anterior mediastinal mass containing soft-tissue, fluid, and fat. Clinical examination was unremarkable. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Benign mediastinal teratoma
Mediastinal goiter
Mediastinal parathyroid adenoma
Mediastinal seminoma
Thymic carcinoma

stem: Which of the following statements regarding mediastinal seminoma is correct?
options: Surgery is the treatment of choice for locally advanced seminomas.
Primary mediastinal seminomas comprise 10 to 15% of malignant mediastinal germ cell tumors.
Primary mediastinal seminomas occur most frequently in men ages 20 to 40 years.
Radiographically, seminomas appear as a homogeneous cystic mass.
Seminomas are uniquely resistant to radiation therapy.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding mediastinal nonseminomatous germ cell tumors (GCTs) is correct?
options: An elevated α-fetal protein (AFP level) is suggestive of an endodermal sinus tumor.
In contrast to pure seminomas, nonseminomatous GCTs carry a better prognosis.
Surgery is the current standard of care for patients with nonseminomatous malignant GCTs.
These tumors are often asymptomatic.
They are predominantly benign.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding primary mediastinal Hodgkin lymphoma is correct?
options: For patients with Hodgkin disease who relapse allogeneic bone marrow transplant (BMT) is superior to autologous BMT.
Lymphocyte-rich subtype represents two thirds of cases of mediastinal Hodgkin disease.
MOPP chemotherapy regimen is superior to ABVD regimen in preventing relapse.
Hodgkin lymphoma represents approximately 50 to 70% of mediastinal lymphomas.
Patients with favorable stage I & II Hodgkin disease have cure rates of < 50% with standard treatment.

stem: A 49-year-old man with fever, cough and chest pain had a chest x-ray that revealed a rounded mass (arrow) that displaced the right primary bronchus superiorly (Figure A). A sagittal T1-weighted magnetic resonance image (Figure B) of the same mass is also shown. Thoracoscopic needle aspiration of the mass showed ciliated, pseudostratified, columnar epithelium. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Bronchogenic cyst
Enterogenous cyst
Lymphangioma
Neuroenteric cyst
Pericardial cyst

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the enterogenous cysts is correct?
options: Enterogenous cysts are associated with multiple vertebral anomalies.
Enterogenous cysts are lined with ciliated, pseudostratified, columnar epithelium.
Enterogenous cysts are identified in the fourth to fifth decade of life.
Enterogenous cysts arise from the ventral foregut.
Enterogenous cysts can be difficult to distinguish from bronchogenic cysts, radiographically.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the pericardial cysts is correct?
options: Pericardial cysts are predominantly acquired.
Pericardial cysts are identified in the first decade of life.
Pericardial cysts are most commonly located at the left cardiophrenic angle.
Pericardial cysts appear as multiloculated masses on CT scan.
Pericardial cysts form as a result of a persistent parietal recess during embryogenesis.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the lymphangiomas is correct?
options: Lymphangiomas are commonly found in teens.
Lymphangiomas are found in the cervical region 75% of the time.
Lymphangiomas in 90% of the cases are associated with chylothorax and hemangiomas.
Lymphangiomatosis is commonly seen in young men.
Lymphangiomas typically are widespread.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the neurogenic tumors is correct?
options: Nerve sheath tumors comprise 40 to 65% % of neurogenic mediastinal masses.
Neurofibromas are firm, encapsulated masses consisting of Schwann cells.
Neurogenic tumors comprise 95% of all mediastinal masses.
Ninety percent of neurogenic tumors are asymptomatic.
Seventy percent to 80% of neurogenic tumors are malignant.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the autonomic ganglionic tumors is correct?
options: Ganglioneuromas are the least benign of the autonomic ganglionic tumors.
Ganglioneuroblastomas are the most common type of neurogenic tumor.
Ninety percent of neuroblastomas arise in the adrenal glands.
On CT scan, 80% of neuroblastomas have calcification.
Treatment of neuroblastomas is predominantly radiotherapy.

stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding chronic fibrosing mediastinal inflammation?
options: Airway obstruction is alleviated by excising granulomatous lymph nodes around airways.
Antifungal therapy is effective treatment.
It is caused by tuberculous infection in the majority of cases.
Unresolved superior vena caval syndrome is the major cause of morbidity.
Venous bypass is rarely indicated.

stem: The Medical Research Council Working Group randomized controlled trial (OEO2) to compare surgical resection with or without preoperative chemotherapy in esophageal cancer patients showed that
options: event free survival was unaffected by preoperative chemotherapy.
overall survival was better in the group that received preoperative chemotherapy.
preoperative chemotherapy reduced median survival.
there was increased incidence of adverse serious events in the group that received preoperative chemotherapy.
there was no difference in microscopically complete resection in the two groups.

stem: Atrial arrhythmias are seen commonly after thoracic surgical procedures. Which of the following statements about atrial fibrillation after esophagectomy is correct?
options: Advanced age is a predictor of postoperative atrial fibrillation after esophagectomy.
Epidural pain management in patients undergoing esophagectomy can potentially reduce the incidence of postoperative atrial fibrillation by increasing the sympathetic tone.
Postoperative atrial fibrillation after esophagectomy is an “innocent bystander”.
Prophylactic digoxin is effective in reducing postoperative atrial fibrillation after esophagectomy.
The incidence of postoperative atrial fibrillation after esophagectomy is less than 10%.

stem: Injury to the recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) has been reported at varying rates after transhiatal and transthoracic esophagectomy. Which of the following statements about RLN injury after esophagectomy is correct?
options: In the majority of the patients the nerve injury is contralateral to the cervical incision.
Neoadjuvant chemoradiation increases the rate of RLN injury.
RLN injury has minimal impact on the overall postoperative well being of the patient.
The incidence of RLN injury appears to be less common after an Ivor-Lewis esophagectomy.
The incidence of RLN injury appears to be less common after transhiatal esophagectomy.

stem: Thoracic duct injury and the resultant chylothorax can be an aggravating and at times difficult problem to take care of following esophagectomy. Chylothorax
options: after esophagectomy even if high output will stop with conservative management.
has a reported incidence of >10% after esophagectomy.
incidence appears to be higher after transhiatal esophagectomy when compared with Ivor-Lewis esophagectomy.
that fails to resolve with conservative management is best treated with left thoracotomy with mass ligation of the tissue between the aorta and the spine.
that is resistant to all treatment strategies is best treated with thoracic duct embolization.

stem: Pulmonary complications are a major source of morbidity and mortality following esophagectomy. Pulmonary complications
options: after esophagectomy are correlated to preoperative FEV1.
after esophagectomy are more commonly seen in patients who have received neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
after esophagectomy are more commonly seen in patients who require a splenectomy at the time of esophageal resection.
have a reported incidence of 50% after esophagectomy.
have been shown to be significantly reduced by postoperative epidural analgesia compared to intravenous analgesia.

stem: Compared to transthoracic esophageal resection the incidence of
options: atrial fibrillation is less after transhiatal esophageal resection.
chylothorax is more after transhiatal esophageal resection.
hoarseness is more after transhiatal esophageal resection.
pulmonary complications is more after transhiatal esophageal resection.
pulmonary complications is the same after transhiatal esophageal resection.

stem: Uncertainty about morbidity and mortality; the occurrence, magnitude, and duration of benefit; and preoperative predictors of benefit from lung-volume reduction surgery led to the conduct of a federally sponsored, multicenter, randomized clinical trial, the National Emphysema Treatment Trial (NETT). In NETT
options: overall mortality was more in the medical treatment group.
improvement in exercise capacity was similar in the two treatment groups at 24 months.
among patients with predominantly upper-lobe emphysema and low exercise capacity, mortality was lower in the medical-therapy group than in the surgical group.
among patients with non-upper-lobe emphysema and high exercise capacity, mortality was higher in the surgery group than in the medical-therapy group
lung-volume-reduction surgery confers an overall survival advantage over medical therapy.

stem: A 58-year-old male was diagnosed with a 4 cm non-small cell lung cancer invading the visceral pleura. According to the seventh edition of TNM classification this patient has a
options: T1a tumor
T1b tumor
T2a tumor
T2b tumor
T3

stem: A 16-year-old soccer player during annual physical examination was found to have an ejection click audible in the aortic area. Echocardiography revealed the presence of a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Which of the following statements regarding bicuspid aortic valve is correct?
options: Endocarditis is the most frequent complication involving patients with BAV.
Fifty percent of patients with BAV will actually develop aortic dissection.
It is inherited in an autosomal dominant fashion with reduced penetrance.
The most common subtype of BAV involves fusion of right and non-coronary cusps.
The prevalence of BAV in the general population is 5%.

stem: A 19-year-old male was admitted to the hospital after sustaining multiple injuries, including sternal fracture, in a motor vehicle accident. An admission echocardiogram revealed a dilated coronary sinus (Figure) with normal right sided filling pressures, raising the suspicion for the presence of a persistent left sided superior vena cava (PLSVC). Which of the following statements regarding PLSVC is correct?
options: Drainage of PLSVC into coronary sinus is of no hemodynamic consequence.
It is formed as a result of persistence of cephalic portion of left superior cardinal vein.
PLSVC is associated with absence of the innominate vein in 95% cases.
PLSVC is the most common congenital vascular anomaly.
The most common subtype of PLSVC is associated with absent right SVC.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) is correct?
options: During fetal development, the preponderance of left ventricular output passes through the ductus arteriosus into the descending aorta.
Fetal patency of the ductus arteriosus is maintained by high fetal oxygen tension.
Histologically, the constitution of the fetal ductus arteriosus differs from that of the contiguous main pulmonary artery and descending aorta.
In normal cardiovascular development, the proximal portion of the left sixth arch persists as the ductus arteriosus.
Premature constriction or closure of ductus arteriosus may lead to left heart failure during fetal life.

stem: Which of the following statement regarding the epidemiology of patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) is correct?
options: PDA has a predilection for males.
PDA is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.
PDA occurs with increased frequency following cytomegalovirus infection during the first trimester of pregnancy.
PDA occurs with increased frequency in Osler-Rendu-Weber syndrome.
PDA occurs with increased frequency in trisomy 21.

stem: Which of the following is a recognised pathophysiological effect of patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)?
options: Decreased catecholamine release
Decreased diastolic blood pressure
Decreased left atrial pressure
Decreased myocardial oxygen demand
Decreased pulmonary vascular resistance

stem: In infants with esophageal atresia and tracheoesophageal fistula (TEF) which of the following statements is true?
options: A circular myotomy should routinely be performed so as to minimize tension on the anastomosis.
Delayed repair with gastric interposition is a reasonable option for most patients.
The fistulous tract should be divided flush with the trachea since a small amount of residual esophageal mucosa will produce excessive tracheal mucous production.
Gastrostomy should be performed following repair of the fistula.
A retropleural approach to the fistula protects against empyema in the event of an anastomotic leak.

stem: Which of the following statements about congenital tracheoesophageal fistula is true?
options: Abdominal distention secondary to gastric and intestinal distention is uncommon in neonates with congenital tracheoesophageal fistulae.
Esophageal atresia with a proximal tracheoesophageal fistula is the most common type encountered.
Free gastroesophageal reflux resulting in chemical pneumonitis is a rare feature of congenital tracheoesophageal fistula.
Respiratory distress is an early sign of esophageal atresia with a distal tracheoesophageal fistula.
The most common presentation is inability to swallow the feeds.

stem: A child is born with a left-sided aortic arch and a Type I esophageal atresia with a gap of 6.2 cm between the proximal and the distal esophagus. options: primary repair via a right thoracotomy immediately.
primary repair via a right thoracotomy at one week.
primary repair via a left thoracotomy at three weeks.
primary repair via a right thoracotomy at six weeks.
colonic interposition at four months.

stem: A 6-year-old child with recurrent chest infections and failure to thrive was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis. Which of the following statements regarding cystic fibrosis is correct?
options: It is an autosomal dominant disease.
It is caused by mutations in the BAC-1 gene.
The commonly accepted explanation for airway disease in cystic fibrosis is the "high volume" hypothesis.
The commonest mutation is the deletion of phenylalanine at codon 508.
The inflammatory response in a patient with cystic fibrosis is 10 times less than a normal person.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the diagnosis of cystic fibrosis is correct?
options: Patients with the cystic fibrosis have raised concentrations of potassium and chloride in the urine.
Sweat concentrations of sodium and chloride < 40 mmol/L is diagnostic of cystic fibrosis in an infant.
Sweat concentrations of sodium and chloride > 60 mmol/L is diagnostic of cystic fibrosis.
The optimal diagnostic test for cystic fibrosis is the measurement of pancreatic juice electrolyte levels.
The optimal diagnostic test for cystic fibrosis is the measurement of sweat potassium levels.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the development of the lung is correct?
options: The basic structure of the gas exchange units of the lung appear in the acinar phase.
The distal airspaces continue to multiply and differentiate into more complex gas exchange units during the pseudoglandular phase.
The embryonic phase encompasses development of the conducting airways.
The lung begins differentiation in the fourth week of gestation.
The lung develops as a dorsal out pouching on the floor of the primitive foregut.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the extralobar pulmonary sequestration (ELS) is correct?
options: ELS are most commonly found on the left side.
ELS is a discrete mass of pulmonary parenchyma existing inside the pleural investment of the lung.
ELS in 80% of cases derives its blood supply from the pulmonary artery.
ELS in 80% of cases drains by the pulmonary venous system.
ELS is related to abnormal expression of the p53 gene.

stem: An anteroposterior radiograph of the chest of a 3-day-old child with respiratory distress shows mild hyperexpansion of the left upper lobe. A diagnosis of congenital lobar emphysema was made. Congenital lobar emphysema
options: is characterised by destruction of alveolar walls with overdistension of alveoli.
is caused by extrinsic compression from a vascular anomaly such as an avalvular pulmonary artery or patent ductus arteriosus.
is the most common cause for a congenital lung mass.
predominantly affects the lower lobes.
presents with cyanosis after birth in 90% of the cases.

stem: Anteroposterior (AP) and lateral radiographs of the chest in a 14-week-old female, with cough and wheeze, demonstrated indistinctness of the tracheal air shadow on the AP view, and anterior bowing of the trachea on the lateral view. options: are rarely detected with prenatal sonography.
arise from dorsal foregut.
in children are predominantly symptomatic.
in the mediastinum frequently communicate with the tracheobronchial tree.
in two-third of the cases are intraparenchymal.

stem: A five-year-old child was brought to the Emergency Department by the parents with symptoms of stridor and dyspnea while lying flat. options: Cystic hygroma
Hemangioma
Lymphoma
Thymoma
Teratoma

stem: Which of the following statements regarding mediastinal masses in children is correct?
options: Most children with mediastinal masses are asymptomatic.
Neurogenic tumors are the most common mediastinal malignancy in children.
Neurogenic tumors are usually located in the anterosuperior mediastinum.
Primary mediastinal tumors and cysts are relatively rare in the pediatric population.
Teratomas are the most common benign lesions.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding neurogenic tumors in children is correct?
options: Ganglioneuromas are composed of both mature and immature Schwann cells.
Ganglioneuroblastomas are highly malignant.
Neuroblastomas are the most common neurogenic tumors in children.
Neurofibromas are well encapsulated.
Overall 5-year survival rate for ganglioneuroblastomas is 88%.

stem: Congenital tracheomalacia is believed to be a consequence of the inadequate maturity of tracheobronchial cartilage, either from premature delivery or from an innate immaturity despite normal gestation. Congenital tracheomalacia
options: is associated with the mucopolysaccharidoses, such as Hunter syndrome and Hurler syndrome.
is predominantly seen in females.
is most commonly associated with protracted endotracheal intubation.
is more common than the acquired form.
persists throughout the life of the affected individual.

stem: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) is a relatively common birth defect associated with high mortality and morbidity. options: most commonly occurs in the anterior retrosternal position.
has a high mortality due to associated cardiac defects.
is associated with Trisomy 13, 18, and 21 and 45,X aneuploidies.
is associated with abnormalities in the vitamin B signalling pathways.
has a high recurrence risk in familial cases.

stem: Numerous techniques for mitral valve reconstruction in children have been reported. These techniques are not always successful in repairing congenitally malformed mitral valves necessitating mitral valve replacement (MVR). In children
options: replacement with mechanical prosthesis precludes re-replacement.
the incidence of heart block after MVR is 1%.
the incidence of prosthetic valve thrombosis, thromboemboli, and anticoagulation-related bleeding necessitating transfusion is nearly 5%.
the most important indication for redo MVR is patient-prosthesis mismatch.
xenografts have better durability compared with caged-ball prostheses in mitral position.

stem: Ebstein’s anomaly is a complex congenital anomaly with a broad anatomic and clinical spectrum. Which of the following is a characteristic feature of Ebstein’s anomaly?

dilation of the left atrioventricular junction (true mitral annulus)
dilation of the atrialized portion of the right ventricle
redundancy, fenestrations, and tethering of the posterior leaflet
superior displacement of the functional annulus (septal>posterior>anterior)

stem: Deletion of chromosome 22q11 is the most frequent known interstitial deletion found in man with an incidence of 1 in 4000 live births. is strongly associated with hypothyroidism.
is inherited as an autosomal recessive disorder.
is characterized by defects in derivatives of the embryonic pharyngeal arches and pouches.
is associated with B-cell mediated immune deficiency.

stem: Hypercyanotic spell is a serious condition in patients with tetralogy of Fallot. Hypercyanotic spell
options: is seen in all patients with tetralogy of Fallot.
is characterised by absence of murmur.
is accompanied by decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance.
is accompanied by increase in systemic vascular resistance.
is best managed by promoting right to left flow across the ventricular septal defect.

stem: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a modified adaptation of conventional cardiopulmonary bypass techniques for prolonged cardiopulmonary support using intrathoracic or extrathoracic cannulation. ECMO support

is only useful in cases where the primary lung injury is accompanied by the presence of oxygen toxicity.
is indicated for oxygenation index > 40 or > 35 for 4 hours.
results in increase in peak and mean blood flow velocities by 30-35%.
results in increase in diastolic blood pressure.

stem: Kawasaki Disease (KD) is a multisystem inflammatory illness of young childhood that can result in acute vasculitis, most strikingly of the coronary arteries. In KD
options: approximately 25% of children develop coronary artery abnormalities.
ITPKC, a positive regulator of T cell activation, confers susceptibility to KD in Japanese populations.
immune complex deposits are observed in inflamed arterial tissue.
primary autoimmune aetiology is most likely.
steroids are the primary therapy of choice.

stem: Congenital defects of the interatrial septum are the most common congenital heart disease presenting in adulthood. Which of the following statements regarding interatrial septal defects is correct?
options: Ostium primum atrial septal defects are considered the severest form in the spectrum of endocardial cushion defects.
Ostium secundum atrial septal defects result from the lack of septation between the pulmonary veins and the superior vena cava or right atrium.
Sinus venosus atrial septal defect is the least common type of atrial septal defect.
Clinically silent atrial septal defects produce a left-to-right shunt.
A pulmonary-to-systemic blood flow ratio (Qp:Qs ratio) of 1:1.5 will cause a patient to be symptomatic.

stem: Transposition of the great arteries (TGA), also referred to as complete transposition, is a congenital cardiac malformation characterised by atrioventricular concordance and ventriculoarterial (VA) discordance. TGA

is associated with noncardiac malformations in 90% cases.
with left ventricular outflow tract obstruction is more commonly seen when the ventricular septum is intact.
is characterised by systemic and pulmonary circulations in series.
-associated central cyanosis is worsened by intravenous prostaglandin E1.

stem: The cardiovascular system is the first organ system to form and function in the vertebrate embryo. Which of the following statements regarding cardiogenesis is correct?
options: The heart tube at the time of its formation is a three-layered structure.
Endothelial-derived cells in the cardiac cushions function to separate the common outflow tract into the pulmonary artery and aorta
Endothelial and hematopoietic cells arise from a common ectodermal precursor, the hemangioblast.
Endoderm-derived endothelial precursors called angioblasts aggregate to form the dorsal and ventral aortae and the vitelline vessels.

stem: The aortopulmonary (AP) window is a congenital malformation characterized by a communication between the ascending aorta and the pulmonary artery in the presence of separate semilunar valves. AP window
options: is rarely associated with other cardiac defects.
between the ascending aorta and the origin of the right pulmonary artery is termed type I.
results in right to left shunt.
closes spontaneously in majority of cases.
type III consists in the anomalous origin of the right pulmonary artery of the aorta.

stem: Congenital tracheal stenosis is a rare disorder characterized by the presence of focal or diffuse complete tracheal cartilage rings, resulting in a fixed tracheal narrowing. Congenital tracheal stenosis
options: is most commonly associated with interrupted aortic arch.
in approximately 50% cases is generalized.
of focal variety usually involves lower one-third.
of focal variety is characterized by narrow distal end of the trachea and bronchi.
when discovered early in life has better prognosis.

stem: Compression and displacement of the trachea and esophagus as a result of anomalous development of the aorta and its branches are not uncommon in the pediatric patient. options: Patients with double aortic arch are usually asymptomatic.
In patients with double aortic arch chest x-ray is diagnostic.
The most common of the aortic arch anomalies is an aberrant left subclavian artery.
An aberrant right subclavian artery rarely causes symptoms.
An aberrant right subclavian artery originates from right aortic arch.

stem: Congenital bronchial atresia is a rare anomaly that results from focal obliteration of a proximal segmental or subsegmental bronchus that lacks communication with the central airways. Congenital bronchial atresia
options: is characterised by abnormal development of structures distal to the atretic bronchi.
more frequently affects upper lobes.
in an adult is seen as a water-density mass.
is almost always symptomatic.
is best diagnosed on plain chest radiograph.

stem: Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is known to trigger a global inflammatory response. Which of the following statements regarding the CPB-induced inflammation is correct?

The anaphylatoxins C3a and C5a cause degranulation of eosinophils with histamine release.
Kallikrein enters a negative feedback loop with factor XIIa.
Plasma kallikrein levels significantly decrease after the administration of heparin.
The neutrophil cell membrane is the primary source of arachidonic acid.

stem: Congenitally corrected transposition is a rare cardiac malformation. Congenitally corrected transposition
options: is characterized by concordant atrioventricular and discordant ventriculo-arterial connections.
has morphologically left ventricle usually positioned to the right.
has abnormal physiology.
does not have recurrence risk in siblings of previously affected children.
patients present with cyanosis in earl infancy.

stem: Complete atrioventricular canal, also referred to as complete atrioventricular septal defect, is an uncommon congenital heart disease. Complete atrioventricular canal
options: is characterised by an ostium primum atrial septal defect, separate atrioventricular valves and a variable deficiency of the ventricular septum inflow.
predominantly affects males.
Rastelli type A has the superior bridging leaflet almost completely adherent to the left ventricle.
Rastelli type B is the most common form of atrioventricular canal.
